prompt.text:
Which of the following monetary policy actions is most likely considered 
expansionary? The central bank:

choices: acts as the lender in a repurchase agreement.
sells government bonds to commercial banks.
raises reserve requirements of commercial banks.

feedback.neutral:
A is correct because if the central bank wishes to increase the supply of money, it 
might buy bonds (usually government bonds) from the banks, with an agreement to 
sell them back at some time in the future. This transaction is known as a repurchase 
agreement. The lender in a repurchase agreement is the party that initially buys the 
bonds and agrees to sell them back at a later point in time. By purchasing bonds from 
banks, the central bank is increasing the money supply, or increasing liquidity, which 
is expansionary.
